rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Trick 1: Henry's law one line: p = KH·x — gas solubility DECREASES with temperature, INCREASES with pressure; scuba diving and soda bottles are the standard applications.  ·  Trick 2: Higher KH → lower solubility (KH is the pressure needed to dissolve unit mole fraction) — the inverse reading earns the mark.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Trick 3: Solid solubility rule of thumb: like dissolves like — polar solutes in polar solvents; solubility usually rises with temperature for endothermic dissolution.  ·  Trick 4: Anoxia at altitude and bends: low pressure → low gas solubility → N2 bubbles in blood — the application 2-marker.  ·  define + example each sub-idea: solubility of gases, solids in liquids.
